newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: SERBIA GRANTS CREDITS FOR LIVESTOCK SECTOR -PAPER.
newsitem.headline: SERBIA GRANTS CREDITS FOR LIVESTOCK SECTOR -PAPER.

text.p: The Serbian government has allocated 54 million German marks of credit for reviving livestock, poultry and dairy production, Belgrade daily Politika reported on Wednesday.

The hard currency credit deals, signed on Tuesday between the Serbian Development Fund and 147 producers in Serbia, carry a four percent annual interest rate and repayment period of two, 10, 15 and 36 months, depending on production cycles.
The loans will be repaid to the Fund through exports of final products and sales on the domestic market, the paper said.
Of the total amount, 20 million marks will be used to breed 10,000 heifers, 14 million for 40,000 sows, 10 million for 10,000 young bulls for export and 10 million for raising poultry.

"As part of economic reforms, the Serbian government has decided to invest 270 million marks in agricultural production this year and to revive and develop livestock breeding with 54 million marks from the Development Fund," Serbian Agriculture Minister Jovan Babovic was quoted as saying.
Livestock breeding is a key segment in Serbia's strategy for development of agriculture and is planned to account for more than 55 percent of total farm production, Babovic said.
Livestock production has declined rapidly over the past few years, primarily due to a lack of turnover and credits.

According to official statistics, cattle numbers dropped from 2.09 million in pre-war 1991 to 1.92 million in 1996, sheep from 3.04 million to 2.65 million and poultry from 30.21 million to 26.45 million.
The number of pigs inched up from 4.35 million in 1991 to 4.44 million last year.

The European Union has approved a quota for exports of 10,000 tonnes of meat from Yugoslavia to its markets. Exports have not yet begun since slaughterhouses are still awaiting permits from the EU Commission.
